claims.source: GAO/NSIAD-95-187, letter of transmittal and scope section
claims.text: GAO conducted its Roswell records review at the request of Representative Steven H. Schiff, working from March 1994 to June 1995.
'RAAF outgoing messages (from Oct. 1946 through Dec. 1949) were destroyed.'
'The document disposition form does not indicate what organization or person destroyed the records and when or under what authority the records were destroyed.'
RAAF administrative records from March 1945 through December 1949 were also destroyed.
The CIA's Executive Director told GAO that a search against the term 'Roswell, New Mexico' in all CIA databases produced no CIA documents related to the crash.

claims.source: GAO/NSIAD-95-187, 'Government Records: Results of a Search for Records Concerning the 1947 Crash Near Roswell, New Mexico,' 28 July 1995
claims.text: GAO reported that RAAF administrative records (March 1945-December 1949) and RAAF outgoing messages (October 1946-December 1949) were destroyed, and that 'the document disposition form does not indicate what organization or person destroyed the records and when or under what authority the records were destroyed.'
GAO's search for government records concerning the Roswell crash 'yielded two records originating in 1947.'
GAO's list of records searched includes 'National Security Agency, Fort Meade, Md. - FOIA records, Citizens Against UFO Secrecy.'

conflicts: The Air Force's own 1994-1997 Roswell reports attributed the events to Project MOGUL and anthropomorphic test dummies; GAO made no finding on the cause and confined itself to the records.

label: Steven H. Schiff
narrative: Schiff is the proof that a single member of Congress asking a records question can produce a durable federal finding. Representing New Mexico's first district, he requested information from the Department of Defense about the 1947 Roswell events in 1993, was routed to the National Archives rather than given an answer, and responded by directing the General Accounting Office to conduct a formal search of government records. GAO reported to him in July 1995 as GAO/NSIAD-95-187. Its finding is the one that matters and is still cited three decades later: Roswell Army Air Field administrative records from March 1945 through December 1949 and RAAF outgoing messages from October 1946 through December 1949 had been destroyed, and 'the document disposition form does not indicate what organization or person destroyed the records and when or under what authority the records were destroyed.' GAO also recorded that only two government records originating in 1947 could be located. Schiff had asked for the paper trail and GAO told him, in the flat language of an audit agency, that the paper trail covering the relevant period had been eliminated by persons unknown under authority unknown. He died in 1998.
